answer: mesa admits a knoll only by a tenure-squared burn: burn opal equal to the square of mesa's total attested tenure at commit. Registration credits one attested epoch before the next read, so batches cannot share the price; the kth clone pays (S+k)^2 opal, and n clones cost the sum of those squares. The bill is opal attached to each knoll's mesa entry; parallel registration only advances one counter. It breaks if tenure transfers, mesa resets the counter, or registration splits across shards.
